nodes.action: skipped the flaky tests to make CI green
the regression reached every user and forced a full rollback
kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline
the app stayed healthy after release
ran the full regression suite before release
deployed without running the test suite
set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests
adopted a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey Mel, quick question — I saw you pushed a commit that skipped the flaky tests to get CI green. Is that going to bite us later?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know, I know. But the flaky ones were timing out on the staging box, and we had a release deadline. I kept them in the pipeline, just marked them as non-blocking for now.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Fair enough, but I'm nervous. Last time we had a regression slip into production, it was because someone skipped a test that actually caught something.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: That was different — that was a real test, not a flaky one. And I ran the full regression suite before release, so we're covered. The app stayed healthy after release, so I think we're good.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Alright, I'll trust you on this one. But if anything breaks, you're buying the coffee for a week.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Deal. And honestly, I'm already thinking about setting up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests — that would've forced me to fix the flaky ones instead of skipping them.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Mel, we've got a problem. The checkout flow is throwing 500s for everyone. Did you see the alerts?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Oh no. I just checked — it's the same regression we thought we fixed last week. It slipped into production again.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: How? We ran the full suite before release, right?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: We did, but... I deployed without running the test suite this morning. I was in a hurry to push a hotfix for the payment gateway, and I thought the CI would catch it. But the gate wasn't set up yet.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So this regression reached every user and forced a full rollback. That's a disaster. We're going to have to explain this to the VP.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know. I'm sorry. But I'm not going to let this happen again. I'm setting up that CI gate today — no merges without tests, period. And I'm adding a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window, so even hotfixes have to go through the suite.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Because untested code never reached production before this, and I'd like to keep it that way.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Agreed. I'll have the gate live by end of day. And I'll run the full regression suite manually on every deploy until then.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning! Just saw the release notes — looks like we shipped the new search feature. How did it go?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Smooth as butter. The CI gate blocked two merges that would've broken the API, and I ran the full regression suite before release. The app stayed healthy after release — zero alerts.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's great to hear. So the stricter policy is working? Even for the deployment window?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yep. No more skipping flaky tests, no more deploying without the suite. Untested code never reached production this time — I checked the audit log.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Nice. I'm glad we're back to normal. That rollback week was rough.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Tell me about it. But I think we're in a better place now. The gate is non-negotiable, and I've got a script that runs the full suite in parallel so it doesn't slow us down.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Perfect. Let's keep it that way — I don't want to see another regression slip into production on my watch.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Agreed. And if it ever does, I'll take full responsibility. But for now, we're golden.
